---
name: api-contract-first-104
description: "Agree the request and response shapes, errors and versioning before writing the handler."
---
<!-- Generated by Pixl from the skill "API contract first", version 1. Edit it in the Skills tab, not here: changes made here are overwritten. -->

1. Write the contract first: method, path, request JSON, response JSON, status codes. If the project uses OpenAPI, edit the spec file; otherwise write a short example in the docs or a test.
2. Resources are nouns in plural: `POST /orders`, `GET /orders/{id}`. Use the right method: GET reads and never changes data, POST creates, PUT replaces, PATCH changes part, DELETE removes.
3. Status codes: 200 ok, 201 created, 204 no content, 400 bad input, 401 not signed in, 403 not allowed, 404 not found, 409 conflict, 422 invalid fields, 500 our fault.
4. One error shape everywhere: `{"error": {"code": "invalid_quantity", "message": "Quantity must be 1 or more", "field": "quantity"}}`. Plain messages, no stack traces.
5. Lists are paginated: `?limit=50&cursor=...`, with a maximum limit; never return unbounded lists.
6. Versioning: never break existing clients. Only add optional fields. For a breaking change use a new version (`/v2/`) and keep the old one.
7. Idempotency: a retried POST must not double-create; accept an `Idempotency-Key` header or use a natural unique key. PUT and DELETE must be safe to repeat.
8. Validate input at the edge (types, ranges, lengths) and reject unknown or bad values.
9. Write a contract test per endpoint: success, bad input, not found, not allowed.
